estandares: Distingo entre lo que hago habitualmente y lo que estoy haciendo en el momento. Hablo de estados y situaciones del pasado con el verbo to be y con have.
competencias: Contrastar presente simple y presente progresivo; describir el pasado con was/were y had; formular preguntas con was/were y expresiones de tiempo pasado; describir el clima y la apariencia física de las personas.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante presenta dos fotos, una de su infancia y otra actual, y escribe un texto corto contrastando cómo era antes (was/were, had) y qué hace o está haciendo ahora.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student presents two photos, one from childhood and one from today, and writes a short text contrasting what they were like (was/were, had) and what they do or are doing now.

lecciones.content_es:
Dos tiempos, dos usos

  • Presente simple: rutinas, hábitos y hechos permanentes. She works at a bank.
  • Presente progresivo: lo que ocurre ahora o en un periodo temporal. She is working from home this week.

Palabras que los delatan

Simple: always, usually, every day, on Mondays, never.
Progresivo: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!

Verbos que casi nunca van en progresivo

Los verbos de estado: know, like, love, hate, want, need, believe, understand, have (cuando significa poseer). Se dice I know the answer, no I am knowing.
lecciones.content_en:
Two tenses, two uses

  • Simple present: routines, habits and permanent facts. She works at a bank.
  • Present progressive: what is happening now or in a temporary period. She is working from home this week.

Signal words

Simple: always, usually, every day, on Mondays, never.
Progressive: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week, Look!

Verbs that rarely take the progressive

State verbs: know, like, love, hate, want, need, believe, understand, have (when it means to own). We say I know the answer, not I am knowing.

lecciones.t: Pasado simple del verbo to be: was / were
lecciones.t_en: Simple past of the verb to be: was / were
lecciones.content_es:
Solo dos formas

  • was: I, he, she, it — I was at home.
  • were: you, we, they — They were happy.

Negativo

wasn't / weren't: She wasn't tired. · We weren't late.

Para qué sirve

  • Estados y descripciones: The movie was boring.
  • Lugar en el pasado: We were in Cartagena last year.
  • Edad: I was ten when I learned to swim.

Ojo

No se necesita did con to be: la negación y la pregunta se hacen con el verbo mismo.
lecciones.content_en:
Only two forms

  • was: I, he, she, it — I was at home.
  • were: you, we, they — They were happy.

Negative

wasn't / weren't: She wasn't tired. · We weren't late.

What it is used for

  • States and descriptions: The movie was boring.
  • Location in the past: We were in Cartagena last year.
  • Age: I was ten when I learned to swim.

Careful

You do not need did with to be: negatives and questions are made with the verb itself.

lecciones.content_es:
Las más usadas

  • yesterday – ayer · the day before yesterday – anteayer
  • last + periodo: last night, last week, last month, last year, last summer
  • ago (después de la cantidad): two days ago, ten years ago
  • in + año: in 2020 · when I was a child

Dónde se ponen

Normalmente al final de la oración: We visited my aunt last weekend. También pueden ir al inicio, con coma: Yesterday, I was very tired.

Ojo con ago

ago va después de la cantidad de tiempo: three years ago, nunca ago three years.
lecciones.content_en:
The most common ones

  • yesterday · the day before yesterday
  • last + period: last night, last week, last month, last year, last summer
  • ago (after the amount): two days ago, ten years ago
  • in + year: in 2020 · when I was a child

Where they go

Usually at the end of the sentence: We visited my aunt last weekend. They can also open the sentence, with a comma: Yesterday, I was very tired.

Careful with ago

ago goes after the amount of time: three years ago, never ago three years.

lecciones.content_es:
Preguntas de sí o no

Se invierte el verbo y el sujeto: Was the movie good? · Were you at school yesterday?

Respuestas cortas: Yes, it was. / No, it wasn't. — Yes, we were. / No, we weren't.

Con question words

Wh- + was/were + sujeto:

  • Where were you last night?
  • Why was she absent?
  • How was the trip?
  • Who was your first teacher? (aquí Who es el sujeto)

Recuerda

Nunca se usa did junto a was/were: Did you were? es incorrecto.
lecciones.content_en:
Yes or no questions

Invert the verb and the subject: Was the movie good? · Were you at school yesterday?

Short answers: Yes, it was. / No, it wasn't. — Yes, we were. / No, we weren't.

With question words

Wh- + was/were + subject:

  • Where were you last night?
  • Why was she absent?
  • How was the trip?
  • Who was your first teacher?

Remember

Never use did together with was/were: Did you were? is wrong.

lecciones.t: Pasado simple del verbo have: had
lecciones.t_en: Simple past of the verb have: had
lecciones.content_es:
Una sola forma

had sirve para todas las personas: I had, you had, she had, they had.

Negativo y pregunta

Aquí sí se usa el auxiliar did, y have vuelve a su forma base:

  • I didn't have breakfast. (no didn't had)
  • Did you have a good weekend?

Usos frecuentes

  • Posesión: We had a small house.
  • Experiencias: I had a great time.
  • Comidas: She had lunch at two.
lecciones.content_en:
One single form

had works for every person: I had, you had, she had, they had.

Negative and question

Here you do use the auxiliary did, and have goes back to its base form:

  • I didn't have breakfast. (not didn't had)
  • Did you have a good weekend?

Common uses

  • Possession: We had a small house.
  • Experiences: I had a great time.
  • Meals: She had lunch at two.

lecciones.content_es:
Describir el clima

What's the weather like? — It's sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy, foggy, snowy.

Temperaturas: hot (caluroso), warm (templado), cool (fresco), cold (frío), freezing (helado).

Sustantivo, adjetivo y verbo

  • Sustantivo: rain, snow, wind, sun
  • Adjetivo: rainy, snowy, windy, sunny
  • Verbo: It's raining. It's snowing.

Frases útiles

It's freezing today! · The weather was terrible yesterday. · It's 25 degrees.
lecciones.content_en:
Describing the weather

What's the weather like? — It's sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, stormy, foggy, snowy.

Temperatures: hot, warm, cool, cold, freezing.

Noun, adjective and verb

  • Noun: rain, snow, wind, sun
  • Adjective: rainy, snowy, windy, sunny
  • Verb: It's raining. It's snowing.

Useful phrases

It's freezing today! · The weather was terrible yesterday. · It's 25 degrees.

lecciones.content_es:
Altura y contextura

tall, short, thin/slim, heavy, strong, athletic.

Cabello

long / short / medium-length + straight / curly / wavy + black / brown / blond / red hair.
She has long curly brown hair.

Cara

eyes: blue, green, brown eyes. glasses (gafas), freckles (pecas), beard (barba), mustache (bigote).

Los dos verbos

  • be + adjetivo: He is tall.
  • have + parte del cuerpo: He has green eyes.

Orden de los adjetivos: tamaño → forma → color. long straight black hair.
lecciones.content_en:
Height and build

tall, short, thin/slim, heavy, strong, athletic.

Hair

long / short / medium-length + straight / curly / wavy + black / brown / blond / red hair.
She has long curly brown hair.

Face

eyes: blue, green, brown eyes. glasses, freckles, beard, mustache.

The two verbs

  • be + adjective: He is tall.
  • have + body feature: He has green eyes.

Adjective order: size → shape → color. long straight black hair.

repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

El periodo enfrenta tres momentos: lo que haces siempre (presente simple), lo que estás haciendo ahora (presente progresivo) y cómo eran las cosas antes (was/were y had).

Puntos gramaticales

  • Verbos de estado (know, like, want) no van en -ing.
  • was para I/he/she/it; were para you/we/they. Sin did.
  • had es igual para todas las personas, pero el negativo y la pregunta sí usan did + have.
  • Expresiones de pasado: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2020.

Vocabulario

Saludos y comandos de clase, clima (sustantivo, adjetivo y verbo) y apariencia física con be y have.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

The term contrasts three moments: what you always do (simple present), what you are doing now (present progressive) and how things were before (was/were and had).

Grammar points

  • State verbs (know, like, want) do not take -ing.
  • was for I/he/she/it; were for you/we/they. No did.
  • had is the same for every person, but negatives and questions do use did + have.
  • Past expressions: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2020.

Vocabulary

Greetings and classroom commands, weather (noun, adjective and verb) and physical appearance with be and have.
